To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BMP-2 is a maternal gene, which acts in the early development as a ventralizing factor.
BMP-2 transcripts were detected during oogenesis, in cleavage stage embryos and during early neurulation.
BMP-2 is expressed maternally and zygotically in Xenopus laeis, and that BMP-2 RNA injection leads to ventral mesodermalization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the early development of the frog Xenopus lae-vis.
the early development of vertebrate embryos, with a special emphasis on the role of extracellular signalling molecules.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the development of vertebrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Xenopus BMP-2 gene, like its closely related counterpart BMP-4, is a dorsalizing signal in the early development.
BMPs are involved in the specification of mesoderm and endoderm and the patterning of the neural tube and the heart.
BMP-2 is not only a mesodermal inducer but also a ventralizing factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BMP-4 and BMP-2 genes are coexpressed in oocytes and early embryos, but that they become differentially regulated during early gastrulation.
BMP-2 is expressed in the early development in a similar pattern like BMP-4 and that it may act as a ventral mesodermalizing factor.
the Xenopus laeviss BMP-2 gene has a complex expression pattern and is expressed during early development in both maternal and zygotic form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMP-2 is expressed during oogenesis, and is expressed in the neural crest, olfactory placode, pineal body, and heart.
the BMP-2 protein has a very specific role in the early development and that this is not the same as BMP-4.
BMP-2 is expressed in the dorsal blastomeres and the dorsal lip during gastrulation and that BMP-2 can ventralize Xenopus embryos.
